abstract: Human Dicer (hDicer) is a multidomain RNase III enzyme central to RNA interference. Precise coordination between different domains in hDicer governs recognition and processing of double-stranded RNA substrate. While recent structural studies reveal distinct apo and dicing conformations, dynamics and energetics basis of hDicer function, particularly the effect of mutations in RNA recognition remains elusive. In this study, we investigate the mechanistic impact of two specific mutations in hDicer, A872T in platform domain and H1549Y in RIIIDa domain, in recognizing pre-miRNA. Our study shows that the wild-type RNA-bound complex exhibits a relatively confined conformational landscape, stable coordination between helicase and PAZ domains, and a persistent protein-RNA interaction network contributing to domain coupling. The mutant, A872T retains near-WT binding energetics but induces altered conformational sampling, domain coordination and long-range communication accompanied by selective redistribution of hDicer-pre-miRNA interaction networks. Conversely, H1549Y induces broader conformational heterogeneity, increased RNA exposure and redistribution of interdomain communication networks. Dynamic residue-network analysis identifies recurrent communication regions that connect mutation-associated perturbations with distal structural regions. This supports a mutation-specific mechanism, where the effect of local sequence alteration propagates through pre-existing intramolecular communication networks to alter domain coupling and RNA-interface organization without requiring global structural destabilization. A872T predominantly exhibits selective network rewiring with energetic compensation, whereas H1549Y produces broader communication and interaction-network redistribution accompanied by weaker energetic stabilization. Given the involvement of Dicer-dependent miRNA dysregulation in neurodegeneration and cancer, our findings provide a structural framework for understanding how domain-specific mutations may influence hDicer function and miRNA processing.
